title: A formatter rewrites a source file in place and it passes through length zero

provenance.evidence: Two readings. `src/main.rs` at inode 190962360 goes 42 -> 0 bytes, then the SAME inode goes 0 -> 52 bytes. No temporary file appears at any reading; the inode never changes.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling

objects.role: src/main.rs, the source file — one identity throughout

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: A formatter fast enough to finish inside one reading is seen as a single Written, which is the folder-watching backend's FIRST declared restriction working exactly as declared — and here it is the SAFE outcome, because the empty state is what gets skipped.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: src/main.rs holds the formatted text. One durable change for one formatter run over one file.
expected.forbidden_note: Mount sequence 2 and folder sequence 1 are the measured zero-length state. A formatter run over a large tree makes this the common case rather than the rare one: every file in the tree is momentarily empty, and a trigger firing mid-run would checkpoint a tree of empty source files.

notes: The formatter and the editor produce the SAME hazard from completely different code: in-place truncate-then-rewrite is not an editor quirk, it is the ordinary shape of `File::create` followed by `write`.

This is the pattern that makes the maximum-uncheckpointed-bytes trigger dangerous. A whole-repository format is thousands of files each passing through zero; a byte-budget trigger that fires without an anchor would checkpoint one of those moments.
